column3: Watcher Mobs in The Deadlands, Atoll of Immolation or The Cauldron
column5: I believe this eyeball twitches to stare at me while I'm not looking. Unsettling, to say the least. Daedric origin, I believe, but which Daedra? Unsure. - Reginus Buca
column6: I took a tome on Daedric oddities from the shelf, and by Mauloch, I think the eye followed my hand straight to the text. As if it was reading it. Has to be a Watcher eyeball, right? Right? - Ugron gro-Thumog
column7: This thing definitely moves of its own accord, but I don't know if that indicates life, or just an unsettling enchantment. I'm obliged to wonder, if this eye can perceive what we're doing, is there someone watching on the other end? - Gabrielle Benele

column5: This armor sheathing bears more than a passing resemblance to the skin of the creatures known as Lurkers. These beings serve the Daedric Prince Hermaeus Mora, and are rarely seen beyond the plane of Apocrypha. - Gabrielle Benele
column6: By examining the edges of this sheathing, I've noted that this skin appears to have been harvested from a living being. Whether this was done willingly or not is hard to tell. - Ugron gro-Thumog
column7: Well noted, Ugron, but the skin lives still. My research indicates that some sort of alchemical treatment might be preserving this sheathing in a state of quasi-life. Further study is required. Unfortunately. - Reginus Buca

column3: Watchlings in The Deadlands or Atoll of Immolation
column5: This has to be one of the most distasteful antiquities I've ever had to catalogue. It's still twitching. This tentacle matches the description of no living being on Nirn. Clearly a Daedric relic of some kind. - Gabrielle Benele
column6: Runes have been etched quite deftly into the soft flesh. Hmm. Hard to make out what this inscription means, but I can make out Lore:Hekem| and Meht. Tentative examination suggests it is from a Daedric Watcher. - Ugron gro-Thumog
column7: Never seen anything quite like it. It appears to have been harvested for some dark purpose. Honestly, it appears ready to crawl across my face and push through my nostril. I'd strongly advise caution. - Reginus Buca

column5: Coils and coils of this thread, definitely made from the sinews of a Daedra. I sense an unpleasant warmth still radiating from the relic. Why a Seeker's corpse would be utilized in such a fashion is hard to fathom. - Gabrielle Benele
column6: I contacted a colleague from the Mages Guild to have a look at this. A great deal of magicka was expended during its creation. According to my associate, close examination of the relic could result in a splitting headache and a long bout of aphasia. - Ugron gro-Thumog
column7: I took some time to reread Elizanev's Treatise on Otherworldly Garments. Apparently, when threaded through a needle and sewn into a piece of linen, this thread will make the linen move and undulate in a distasteful and organic fashion. Horrific! - Reginus Buca

column3: Gravelight Sentry in Imperial City Prison
column5: A most distressing relic, I must say. This thing is still leaking ocular fluid? It is not an eye from a mortal race, I can tell you that. Leaving further examination for colleagues with stronger stomachs. - Gabrielle Benele
column6: I can confirm this unusual relic comes from no creature of Nirn. My assumption is that it might be from a Daedric Watcher, but that would be pure conjecture. I imagine it has a deeply unpleasant smell. - Ugron gro-Thumog
column7: The normally soft and pliable sclera has a hard, almost keratin-esque quality to it. I wouldn't advise handling it with bare hands. Objects like this often leave stains that are impossible to wash off. - Reginus Buca
